title: Self-Contained Foundations
content: Defines `altFactTerm(k) = (-1)^k / k!` and `altFactPartialSum(n) = ∑_{k=0}^n altFactTerm(k)`. Proves factorial positivity helpers and the successor splitting `altFactPartialSum(n+1) = altFactPartialSum(n) + altFactTerm(n+1)`. Also establishes summability of `altFactTerm` via `summable_pow_div_factorial` and the exponential identity $e^{-1} = \sum_k altFactTerm(k)$ using `NormedSpace.exp_eq_tsum`.

title: Core Identity: D(n) = n! · Partial Sum
content: Proves `numDerangements_eq_factorial_mul_altSum`: $D(n) = n! \cdot S_n$ by strong induction using the derangement recurrence $D(n+2) = (n+1)(D(n+1) + D(n))$. The algebraic manipulation verifies that both sides satisfy the same recurrence. Then `derangements_div_factorial` gives $D(n)/n! = S_n$ by dividing through.
mathContext: $D(n) = n! \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{(-1)^k}{k!}$ proved by strong induction on $n$, using $D(n+2) = (n+1)(D(n+1) + D(n))$

title: Tail Splitting for Infinite Series
content: Proves that the infinite sum splits as $\sum_k a_k = \sum_{k<N} a_k + \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_{N+k}$ by induction on $N$. Uses `Summable.tsum_eq_zero_add` to peel off the first term of the shifted tail. This is the key tool connecting partial sums to the full series, enabling the closed-form error identity.

title: Alternating Partial Sum Bounds
content: Two key lemmas via strong induction: (1) `alt_partial_sum_nonneg` — partial sums of the shifted alternating series $\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} (-1)^k/(m+k)!$ are non-negative; (2) `alt_partial_sum_le_first` — they are bounded above by the first term $1/m!$. Both use the pairing technique: consecutive terms $(a_{2j}, a_{2j+1})$ have non-negative sum since $1/(m+2j)! \geq 1/(m+2j+1)!$. These pass to the infinite sum via `ge_of_tendsto` and `le_of_tendsto`.
mathContext: $0 \leq \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \frac{(-1)^k}{(m+k)!} \leq \frac{1}{m!}$ for all $N$, by pairing consecutive terms: $\frac{1}{(m+2j)!} - \frac{1}{(m+2j+1)!} \geq 0$

title: Error Tail Sum: Definition and Properties
content: Defines `errorTailSum(m) = ∑' k, (-1)^k/(m+k)!` and proves four fundamental properties: (1) non-negativity from the partial sum bound; (2) upper bound $\leq 1/m!$; (3) the elegant recurrence $T(m) = 1/m! - T(m+1)$, proved by splitting off the first term and factoring $(-1)$; (4) strict positivity for all $m$, where the case $m \geq 1$ uses $1/(m+1)! < 1/m!$ and $m = 0$ reduces via double application of the recurrence to $T(2) > 0$.

title: Factoring the Alternating Sign
content: Proves `tail_eq_signed`: the tail $\sum_k a_{m+k} = (-1)^m \cdot T(m)$. Factors $(-1)^{m+k} = (-1)^m \cdot (-1)^k$ using `pow_add`, then pulls out the constant factor via `tsum_mul_left`. This is the bridge between the raw series tail and the always-positive error tail sum.

title: Main Theorem: Closed-Form Error Identity
content: The central result: $D(n)/n! - 1/e = (-1)^n \cdot T(n+1)$. The proof combines three ingredients: (a) $D(n)/n! = S_n$ from the core identity, (b) $e^{-1} = \sum_k a_k$, (c) $S_n - \sum a_k = -(\text{tail at } n+1) = -(-1)^{n+1} T(n+1) = (-1)^n T(n+1)$. Since $T(n+1) > 0$ always, the sign of the error is purely determined by $(-1)^n$.

title: Error Recurrence
content: Proves that the derangement error at $n+1$ equals the error at $n$ plus $(-1)^{n+1}/(n+1)!$: adding one more term of the alternating series. This follows directly from $S_{n+1} = S_n + a_{n+1}$ and is completely independent of the error tail sum machinery.

title: Strict Sign Alternation
content: Two clean corollaries of the closed-form identity: (1) for even $n$, $(-1)^{2n} = 1$ so $D(2n)/(2n)! - 1/e = T(2n+1) > 0$, hence $D(2n)/(2n)! > 1/e$; (2) for odd $n$, $(-1)^{2n+1} = -1$ so the error is $-T(2n+2) < 0$. This gives the precise interlacing pattern: $D(n)/n!$ strictly alternates above and below $1/e$.

title: Normalized Error Limit: Asymptotic Precision
content: Proves $(-1)^n (D(n)/n! - 1/e) \cdot (n+1)! \to 1$. The proof first simplifies to $T(n+1) \cdot (n+1)!$ using the closed form and $(-1)^{2n} = 1$. Then squeezes: upper bound $T(n+1) \cdot (n+1)! \leq 1$ from $T(m) \leq 1/m!$, and lower bound $\geq 1 - 1/(n+2)$ from $T(m) \geq 1/m! - 1/(m+1)!$. Both bounds tend to 1. Uses the $\varepsilon$-$N$ definition via `Metric.tendsto_atTop`.

title: Concrete Values: n = 0 and n = 1
content: Instantiates the sign alternation at the two smallest cases: $D(0)/0! = 1 > 1/e$ (there is 1 derangement of the empty set, and $1 > 1/e \approx 0.368$) and $D(1)/1! = 0 < 1/e$ (no derangement of a singleton). These are direct applications of `error_strict_pos_even 0` and `error_strict_neg_odd 0`.
